This fable refers to the place, Cwm Caw Lwyd , regarding which the writer says:
“With regard to the Cwm Caw Lwyd , there is a still extant fable entitled Creaduriaid Hir Hoedlog (i.e., the long-lived ancestors), which seems to be a composition of no modern date.

At present the moral of it cannot be elucidated; but it seems that, in one respect, it was intended to represent the solitariness of this place, inhabited only by the weeping owl from remote antiquity; and certainly it is the most solitary and romantic retreat that the mind of man could imagine.”
The writer says his is a “literal translation of the story, according to the Welsh phraseology”.
